newsitem.title: GERMANY: US rate worries help push German debt market lower.
newsitem.headline: US rate worries help push German debt market lower.

text.p: German Bunds and futures ended the week on a softer note unable to escape the U.S. Treasury market's losses.

Trading down 16 basis points at 100.45 at 1514 GMT, the June Bund futures contract had dipped as low at 100.25 in late afternoon, following the U.S. market's losses and as traders were squaring positions.

Dealers said the U.S. market is expected to be weighed down by ongoing jitters that next week's slew of economic data will show a much stronger economy which might prompt the Fed to once again raise interest rates.

After the Bund future failed to close a gap between 100.53 and 100.60 points, dealers said it was logical that prices would drift lower. "Everyone who had longs was trying to close them before the weekend," a dealer said.
Should the U.S. Treasury market continue to fall further, then the Bund futures contract has room to drop back to the 100 points level, dealers predicted.
While volume in the futures contract was fairly strong, dealers said there was very little happening on the cash side. "There is virtually nothing going on here," a dealer remarked.
Dealers said comments from Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen about Europe's currency union were rather contradictory but had no direct impact on the market.

Kohl warned that Germany would never accept a delay in the EMU timetable, which states the currency union should begin on January 1, 1999. But Jochimsen said that a delay might be an option to consider. He also said the criteria must not be watered down.
